chemical: Apply azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil fungicide at first sign, per label.
Repeat on a 7–14 day schedule during wet weather; observe pre-harvest intervals.
blight.name: Blight (edge scorch / early blight type)
organic: Remove badly affected leaves and burn or bag them.
Mulch the soil to prevent splash-back of spores onto foliage.
Spray potassium bicarbonate or horsetail-extract tea every 7 days.
blight.summary: Darkened, scorched leaf margins — blight spreads fast in warm, wet weather. Isolate and treat promptly.

chemical: Optional preventive copper-based spray before the rainy season, per label.
healthy.name: Healthy leaf
organic: Continue regular crop rotation and remove fallen debris.
Water at the base of plants in the morning to keep foliage dry.
Apply compost or well-rotted manure to keep plants vigorous.
healthy.summary: No disease detected. Keep up good crop hygiene to stay that way.

chemical: Apply a chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicide per label instructions.
For bacterial spot, use a copper-based bactericide; rotate modes of action.
leaf_spot.name: Leaf spot (fungal/bacterial lesions)
organic: Prune and destroy affected leaves; do not compost them.
Improve air circulation by spacing plants and weeding.
Spray neem oil (2%) or a baking-soda solution (1 tsp/L water) weekly.
leaf_spot.summary: Circular brown lesions with yellow halos — typical of fungal or bacterial leaf spot. Act early to stop spread.

chemical: No cure exists; use systemic insecticides (e.g., imidacloprid) only to control insect vectors, per label.
Follow local regulations — some regions restrict neonicotinoids.
mosaic.name: Mosaic virus (yellowing / mottling)
organic: Rogue out (uproot and destroy) severely infected plants immediately.
Control aphids/whiteflies with insecticidal soap or neem oil.
Disinfect tools with 10% bleach between plants; plant resistant varieties next season.
mosaic.summary: Yellow mottled pattern suggests a mosaic virus. Viruses cannot be cured — focus on containment and vector control.
